edges.description: Disrupted left-right axis specification. Not "reversed": reversal is situs inversus specifically, whereas heterotaxy is the discordant or isomeric arrangement this cohort actually shows.
Cardiovascular malformation arising downstream of the laterality defect.
Pre-streak deletion reproduces reversed left-right patterning with aortic arch artery defects, and the staged design localises the requirement to before symmetry break.
edges.limitations: The staging is mouse-specific and cannot be transferred directly to a human developmental timetable. The model also does not address why human patients retain residual MEGF8 function, since the deletions here are complete.

edges.description: Deleting Megf8 in any cardiac lineage failed to produce cardiovascular defects. This is a substantive negative result, not a missing experiment: it is what shows the cardiac disease is not caused by a cardiac requirement for MEGF8, and is instead downstream of the laterality defect.
edges.limitations: The negative result constrains where MEGF8 is required but does not itself prove the laterality-to-heart causal route, which the authors state as an indication rather than a demonstration. A conditional approach also cannot exclude a requirement below the detection threshold of the phenotyping used.

nodes.description: Failure of ubiquitin-mediated BMPR1A turnover leads to receptor accumulation and canonical BMP-SMAD1/5/9 hyperactivation, accelerating osteogenic differentiation of cranial mesenchyme and closing the cranial sutures prematurely. This arm is Hedgehog-independent: the cranial phenotype is refractory to Hedgehog blockade and is selectively rescued by BMP type I receptor inhibition. It is also the point at which MEGF8 and RAB23 diverge mechanistically despite converging on a shared phenotype, RAB23 acting through FGF-ERK instead.

nodes.description: Congenital heart disease in 10 of 15 reported patients. The specific lesions differ between series and this matters: the 2012 series reported dextrocardia and transposition of the great arteries, but the 2024 cohort states plainly that NONE of its eight individuals had dextrocardia. This entry therefore does not assert dextrocardia or transposition as characteristic of CRPT2, only congenital heart disease as a class.

nodes.description: Abnormal establishment of the left-right axis. The 2012 five-patient series reported complete situs inversus, dextrocardia or transposition of the great arteries in three of its cases; the 2024 eight-patient cohort found none of those, reporting left atrial isomerism, abdominal situs inversus, polysplenia and bowel malrotation instead. The two cohorts are recorded as they stand rather than averaged, which is why the phenotype is bound to the broader Heterotaxy term. Mouse conditional-deletion work places the requirement remarkably early: deletion at embryonic day 6.5, before symmetry break, produces laterality and aortic arch defects, whereas deletion at E7.5 does not, and no cardiac-lineage-restricted deletion produces cardiovascular defects at all. The cardiovascular disease therefore appears to be a downstream consequence of the laterality defect rather than an independent cardiac requirement for MEGF8.

nodes.description: Laterality defects as a class, present in 7 of 15 reported CRPT2 patients and rare in CRPT1 - the second discriminating feature between the subtypes. Bound to Heterotaxy rather than Situs inversus totalis because that is the population the 7/15 fraction was measured over, and because the 2024 cohort reports left atrial isomerism, abdominal situs inversus, polysplenia and bowel malrotation with NO complete situs inversus and no dextrocardia. The feature is also incompletely penetrant: 8 of 15 patients have no laterality defect at all.

nodes.description: Biallelic MEGF8 variants reduce the activity of a multidomain transmembrane protein that restrains two distinct signalling pathways. Reported alleles include nonsense, missense and splice-site changes, and the missense alleles are hypomorphic rather than null: in a zebrafish rescue assay they provide only weak rescue of a Megf8-knockdown gastrulation phenotype. No patient carries two complete loss-of-function alleles, which is interpreted as indicating that some residual MEGF8 function is required for survival.
